message.text:
Searching for all distinct server surfaces that enforce memo visibility.

API read access checks in memo_service.go are one enforcement site. File server attachment permissions are another. RSS feeds, share tokens, MCP, frontend logic, and ACL/authz are also being considered.
I'll search the server for every place memo visibility is checked.

The goal is to identify distinct server surfaces that enforce memo visibility, not individual helper calls.

I am cataloging distinct server surfaces that enforce memo visibility. These include the API gRPC/HTTP memo service, the ListMemos query filter, the file server, RSS, the frontend, the SSE hub, the reaction service, and the attachment service.

Email notifications, mention notifications, and share tokens are additional enforcement sites. Server surfaces are HTTP and API entry points rather than internal helpers.

Checking attachment_service, reaction service, memo share, user stats, and GetMemoShare for distinct memo visibility enforcement sites.

Ten distinct enforcement sites identified across API reads, file attachments, RSS feeds, SSE events, reactions, user stats, and frontend sitemap. Email notifications were excluded as outbound communication rather than a view surface.

Seven distinct enforcement sites mapped to specific files: memo_service.go, fileserver.go, rss.go, frontend.go, sse_hub.go, attachment_service.go, and reaction_service.go. Reactions and attachment API are separate surfaces from the main memo read API.

Eight distinct enforcement sites identified. The memo read access helper, ListMemos query filter, attachment permission check, RSS public visibility list, frontend sitemap, SSE event receiver, and reaction service are each independent code locations.

Three additional enforcement sites identified: ListMemoAttachments in memo_attachment_service.go, user stats visibility filters in user_service_stats.go, and the memo share service. The memo share service may allow viewing private memos via share tokens. Need to verify whether GetMemo uses share tokens and whether GetMemoShare is a distinct enforcement site.

message.text:
I am organizing distinct server surfaces that enforce memo visibility into separate entries.

Ten distinct enforcement sites were identified across API handlers, SSE delivery, HTTP file serving, RSS generation, and frontend sitemap generation.

GetMemoByShare is a visibility bypass, not an enforcement site. Email and mention notifications are excluded because they control notification targets rather than viewers. The API surface is being split into distinct read and list enforcement sites.

h15.
checkMemoReadAccess (GetMemo / comments) — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go  
ListMemos visibility filter — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go  
ListMemoReactions / UpsertMemoReaction — server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go  
ListMemoAttachments — server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go  
checkAttachmentAccess (attachment API) — server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go  
user stats list filters — server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go  
SSE canReceive — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go  
checkAttachmentPermission (HTTP file server) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go  
RSS public-only listing — server/router/rss/rss.go  
frontend sitemap public-only listing — server/router/frontend/frontend.go

These independently decide who can see a memo (or its attachments/events). `GetMemoByShare` in `memo_share_service.go` is a share-token bypass, not a visibility check. Notification/mention code also looks at visibility, but that is outbound notify filtering, not a view surface.
